---
title: "Model support for post estimation"
description: "Check model capabilities and the additional data, weight, and design restrictions of each operation."
sidebar: reference
---

An inherited method is not necessarily supported by every estimator. Each fit
publishes [`fit.capabilities`](/reference/estimation.state.Capabilities.qmd),
which methods check before doing their work. The table below is generated
from the current implementation for representative fits.

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
from dataclasses import asdict

import pandas as pd
import pyfixest as pf

data = pf.get_data(N=200, seed=1234)
data["binary_outcome"] = (data["Y"] > 0).astype(int)
fits = {
    "OLS": pf.feols("Y ~ X1 + X2 | f1", data),
    "IV": pf.feols("Y ~ X2 + [X1 ~ Z1] | f1", data),
    "Poisson": pf.fepois("Y ~ X1 | f1", pf.get_data(N=200, model="Fepois")),
    "GLM logit": pf.feglm("binary_outcome ~ X1", data, family="logit"),
    "Quantile": pf.quantreg("Y ~ X1", data),
}
labels = {
    "covariance_update": "Change covariance after fitting",
    "crv3_inference": "CRV3 covariance",
    "hac_inference": "NW and DK covariance",
    "multiway_clustering": "Multiway clustering",
    "wildboottest": "Wild bootstrap",
    "cluster_causal_variance": "Causal cluster variance",
    "decomposition": "Gelbach decomposition",
    "prediction": "Point prediction",
    "fixed_effect_recovery": "Fixed-effect recovery",
    "randomization_inference": "Randomization inference",
    "sherman_morrison_update": "Coefficient update",
    "anytime_valid_inference": "Anytime-valid inference",
}
support = pd.DataFrame({name: asdict(fit.capabilities) for name, fit in fits.items()})
support = support.rename(index=labels).map(lambda value: "Yes" if value else "No")
print(support.to_markdown())
```

These are model-class capabilities. A **Yes** still requires the applicable
design and retained state:

| Operation | Additional restrictions and interpretation |
| --- | --- |
| [`predict()`](/reference/estimation.models.feols_.Feols.predict.qmd) | Prediction errors and intervals require an unweighted OLS model without absorbed fixed effects. GLM point predictions default to link scale; GLM interval arguments are currently ignored. |
| [`fixef()`](/reference/estimation.models.feols_.Feols.fixef.qmd) | Requires absorbed fixed effects and retained inputs. Individual levels depend on normalization; GLM effects are on link scale. |
| [`wildboottest()`](/reference/estimation.models.feols_.Feols.wildboottest.qmd) | Unweighted OLS, with supported one-way clustering and the optional `wildboottest` dependency. |
| [`ritest()`](/reference/estimation.models.feols_.Feols.ritest.qmd) | Supported OLS and Poisson paths reject observation weights; resampling and retained-data requirements apply. |
| [`ccv()`](/reference/estimation.models.feols_.Feols.ccv.qmd) | Binary treatment, no absorbed fixed effects, and no observation weights. |
| [`decompose()`](/reference/estimation.models.feols_.Feols.decompose.qmd) | Analytic weights are unsupported. Frequency weights require `only_coef=True`; clustered bootstrap supports one cluster variable. Retained-data requirements depend on fixed effects and clustering. |
| [`update()`](/reference/estimation.models.feols_.Feols.update.qmd) | No absorbed fixed effects or observation weights. Returns new coefficients; it does not append observations to the fitted result. |
| SAVI methods | No absorbed fixed effects or observation weights, with supported IID or heteroskedasticity-robust covariance. See [anytime-valid inference](/how-to/anytime-valid-inference.qmd). |
| Covariance estimators | `HC2`/`HC3` require an eligible model without absorbed fixed effects. Quantile regression has its own inference choices and only one-way clustering. |

Basic coefficient accessors and ordinary confidence intervals are available
on the standard result classes. [Storage options](/reference-guide/model-storage.qmd)
can remove state needed by residuals, prediction, refits, or covariance updates.

Difference-in-differences results have additional contracts. DID2S covariance
includes first-stage estimation, so change its cluster specification by
refitting with `cluster=` rather than calling `.vcov()`. DID2S results also
reject ordinary point prediction and resampling procedures that cannot replay
the two-stage estimator. LPDID and saturated aggregation have their own result
interfaces; see the [DiD tutorial](/tutorials/difference-in-differences.qmd).

See also [fitted results](/reference-guide/fitted-results.qmd) and
[errors and remedies](/reference-guide/errors.qmd).
